title: World contours and exposure projections
question: How can the current samples be placed in historical reach context?
accomplishment: Rebuilt Figure 2 with matched three- and four-campaign observed-equivalent projections, including the 2019 1% high-psum sample.
limit: The historical contour survey is incomplete for 2026; exposure scaling and borrowed 2019 response inputs do not establish future sensitivity.

title: Consolidated analysis note v5.0.5
question: Where is the long-form baseline procedure and its earlier study history?
accomplishment: Integrated geometry, exposure/echo studies, local results, and a bounded binning check into the 252-page note. The September language revision preserved the numerical results.
limit: This baseline predates the new v6 template choices; later conditional studies do not silently replace its nominal results.

title: Common coupling and alternative rate models
question: How much does the assumed relationship between campaign rates matter?
accomplishment: Compared shared coupling, independent nonnegative amplitudes, power-law and exponential rate descriptions at 92 MeV, with parameter covariance bands.
limit: These are different pointwise tests. Selecting a model or mass requires additional calibration; relaxed rates do not define a unique combined coupling limit.

title: Projected upper limits and GP echoes
question: What structures could an injected excess produce in future limit scans?
accomplishment: Reused 15 scenarios and 300 Poisson spectra to map conditional upper-limit depressions and neighboring GP response features.
limit: These are source-dependent forecasts, not observed full-2021 data or guaranteed future structures.

title: Angular acceptance illustration
question: Why does the characteristic low-mass scale rise with beam energy?
accomplishment: Derived the boosted two-body angular model and separated the 15 mrad inner-gap scale from an illustrative outer angular cap.
limit: The 70 mrad cap is illustrative, and a selected-spectrum overlay is not a detector-efficiency measurement.

title: Geometry and magnetic transport
question: What changes when tracks are propagated through the actual field and sensor geometry?
accomplishment: Replaced the outer-angle surrogate with pinned field maps, sensor rectangles, and campaign-specific hit requirements; supplied reusable geometry and response plates.
limit: Conditional decay and hit fractions omit the full production distribution, reconstruction/selection efficiency, and detector systematics.

title: Local mapping, stress response and spacing
question: Which effects change an apparent local excess?
accomplishment: Separated grid spacing, binning, window width, source offsets, exposure scaling, and reference-standardized response; retained failed and historical-subset checks.
limit: A stress-centered coordinate is not a calibrated physical significance; legacy full-fit dependencies are documented.

title: Alternative background sources
question: Can a different source remove deterministic bias without hiding signal?
accomplishment: Compared frozen 2016 background constructions and showed that lower stress bias can coexist with source-building signal absorption; unsuccessful sources remain recorded.
limit: Sources estimated from the observed data are not independent controls; incomplete or failed source ensembles do not receive tail probabilities.

title: Coherent nominal-GP significance fields
question: How can the scan-wide trial effect preserve correlations?
accomplishment: Built conditional response fields, compared 200,000 Gaussian-field draws with 256 complete Poisson spectra per campaign, and separated full-union from common-overlap searches.
limit: Reference-local centering/scaling is explicit; source uncertainty and selection among searches are outside this calibration.

title: Resolution and global-probability explanation
question: Why is the number of scan points not the effective number of trials?
accomplishment: Explained covariance, threshold-dependent effective counts, upcrossing comparisons, and the distinction between a discovery tail and a 90% CLs limit using saved fields.
limit: Resolution-count and upcrossing comparisons do not replace the fitted correlated-scan probability.

title: Combination methods and window widths
question: How do shared coupling, Fisher and Stouffer compare under matched scan choices?
accomplishment: Kept each combination rule, width (2.25-2.6 reference sigma), search domain, and reach definition separate while preserving coherent mass correlations.
limit: Method/width selection is not globally calibrated; a probability combination without a signal-rate model does not yield a physical combined coupling limit.

title: Common mass with independent amplitudes
question: Does a common mass remain interesting when campaign amplitudes are free?
accomplishment: Tested a common-mass statistic with independent positive amplitudes and a separate mass-coherence diagnostic. The nominal full-domain direct global count is 7/256 (add-one p=0.03113).
limit: This is a different hypothesis from common coupling. The 80-105 MeV diagnostic is post hoc; zero local exceedances are finite-sample bounds.

title: Consolidated calibration review
question: Which probability comparisons answer the same statistical question?
accomplishment: Documented raw versus reference-standardized ordering, same-field upcrossing comparisons, failures of a simple correlation-cut rule, and limitations of historical-source transfer.
limit: Different orderings are not choices to optimize after seeing the data; no new physical-significance calibration or width choice is certified.

title: Saved-result statistical perspective
question: What follow-up would most clearly distinguish rate consistency from chance structure?
accomplishment: Organized the existing 90-93 MeV and 65-67 MeV evidence around replication, common-rate consistency and additional 2021 data.
limit: This is a statistical reading of saved results, not an independent experimental certification or a new likelihood fit.

title: Fixed background inside the likelihood
question: What happens when the predicted background is held fixed during signal extraction?
accomplishment: Added C=0 likelihood fits and 256 complete conditional toy scans, while retaining count-dependent GP sideband conditioning for every spectrum.
limit: A fixed generating source and a fixed likelihood background are different operations. Small asymptotic p-values require comparison with direct complete-toy tails.

title: Unshifted local and raw-maximum global scans
question: What do the conventional raw local curves say before reference centering?
accomplishment: Reproduced 1,310 archived coordinates with Z=max(r,0). Local peaks include 2016: 90.5 MeV, Z=3.4525; shared coupling: 66 MeV, Z=2.7602.
limit: These are local asymptotic values. The raw-maximum global calculation has a frozen-source scope and differs from a reference-standardized ordering.

title: Controlled Gaussian-tail perturbations
question: How much does a modest tail change affect matched-window observed limits?
accomplishment: Preserved the central Gaussian shape and compared exact-bin-integrated tail alternatives with fresh matching Gaussian references across all three campaigns.
limit: The enlarged-window comparison also changes the GP sidebands. Small effects for this tail family do not imply robustness to broad native MC shapes.

title: Fixed-mass offset versus positive scan maximum
question: Is a positive null maximum evidence of estimator bias?
accomplishment: Separated the expected positive scan maximum from a genuine fixed-mass signed-root offset. At 78 MeV the toy mean is 0.548; the source-conditional full-scan tail is 0.25092.
limit: This is conditional on the fitted generating source. It does not establish background adequacy, unconditional coverage, or discovery calibration.

title: Native 2021 MC shapes and windows
question: How do the supplied reconstructed MC distributions differ from Gaussian signals?
accomplishment: Mapped broad tails, displaced cores, native templates, neighboring-template interpolation, and MC-centered window comparisons; preserved the production/selection audit.
limit: The all-selected MC is not established as a pure resonance response. Selection equivalence and physical coupling normalization remain qualified.

title: Exact-N MC injection and recovery
question: Does moving the extraction window to the MC core recover the full signal?
accomplishment: Final 40-toy release: 1,760 injected spectra and 3,520 primary fits. At N=30,000, paired responses span 71.5-89.5% (pole) and 78.0-93.8% (shifted).
limit: Raw recovery and paired response differ. The 260 MeV extension uses a 250 MeV kernel anchor; finite conditional containment is not coverage certification.

title: Fixed expected yield and reference matching
question: What should be held fixed in an injection performance test?
accomplishment: Distinguished per-toy reference-error matching, fixed expected yield, and exact-N injections; audited the saved baseline and defined expected-yield pulls.
limit: This is a design/audit study, not a new HPS toy ensemble or proof that matching corrects bias.

title: 100-pilot / 100-evaluation 2021 study
question: How do Gaussian and native-MC responses compare at the same expected yield?
accomplishment: Completed 2,000 pilot and 8,000 evaluation fits with no failed rows. At z=5, paired response is 0.961-0.978 for Gaussian and 0.716-0.894 for native MC.
limit: Expected signal is fixed by an independent Gaussian pilot; realized Poisson totals fluctuate. The source, kernels and templates are fixed.

title: 2016 exposure and calibration transfer
question: Can a 10% offset simply be scaled to the full exposure?
accomplishment: Completed independent pilot/calibration/evaluation cohorts and found nontrivial failures of offset scaling and nominal-to-stress transfer; same-source affine corrections reduce mean pulls.
limit: A fitted yield in one observed sample is not an ensemble bias. Offset subtraction cannot restore response or establish transferable coverage.

title: Unified 2021 procedure
question: How do core shifting, response, inference and observed scans fit together?
accomplishment: Connected null calibration, MC-generated/Gaussian-extracted response, finite-grid inference and observed combinations. Retained the primary matched +/-2.25 reference-sigma mask without an added guard.
limit: Core shifts do not produce unit response. Empty, zero-only or censored accepted grids are not precise continuous physical upper limits.

title: Standalone 2021 reader's note
question: Where can the complete 2021 narrative and follow-ups be read in one place?
accomplishment: Created the 56-page integrated note: readable main procedure, v16 TC/UC shapes, template/window tests, leakage controls, observed morph fits and combined scans.
limit: Many appendices reuse earlier results. Do not count them as independent replications; uncertainty methods and normalization qualifications are retained.

title: v16 templates and fit-window study
question: Which full-signal template/window combinations improve extraction?
accomplishment: Compared shifted Gaussian, common aligned, neighboring-MC and direct-MC templates using tuning then independent calibration/evaluation. Common starter won the frozen tuning score; the morph is a separate candidate.
limit: Improved response is not a universal limit improvement. Starter windows leave training contamination, and finite-grid rejection/empty-set accounting matters.

title: Controlled training-contamination test
question: How much of the response loss is caused by signal in the GP sidebands?
accomplishment: At 100/160/220 MeV, removing only training-bin signal changes direct-MC response from 0.959/0.950/0.909 to 1.001/0.997/1.000.
limit: This diagnostic uses the same saved draws and a control unavailable in real data. Leakage fraction and lost fitted yield are distinct quantities.

title: Observed 2021 morphed-template extraction
question: How do the new templates describe the observed local regions?
accomplishment: Completed 543 observed fits and selected-region toy checks at 67, 79, 185 and 226 MeV; provided detailed count, residual and standardized-residual panels.
limit: Masses were selected from the scan. Local checks are not global probabilities; the deficit's empty accepted set is not a zero physical limit.

title: Joint scan with 2021 MC only
question: What changes in the common-coupling fit when only the 2021 template is updated?
accomplishment: The combined local minimum moves to 68 MeV with asymptotic Z=2.910 and p=0.001806; older campaigns remain unchanged.
limit: Zero of 1,000 fixed-mass toy exceedances gives a finite rank floor, not zero probability. This release has no global calibration.

title: 2016 already-smeared MC catalogue
question: Does 2016 need the same signal-shift model as 2021?
accomplishment: Characterized 29 supplied histograms. Qualified 40-175 MeV cores shift down by 0.08-1.02 MeV; 89.2-93.7% lies within two fitted core widths. Neighbor interpolation has smaller held-out CDF discrepancies than common/Gaussian shapes.
limit: 30 and 35 MeV are diagnostic-only; 150 MeV is missing. Use the supplied FEE-smeared/scaled histogram without extra smearing; shape agreement is not efficiency validation.

title: 2016 and joint MC extraction
question: What changes when 2016 also uses its native MC response?
accomplishment: Added 2016-only and common-coupling MC scans with full normalization. At 91 MeV, local asymptotic p=0.000196 differs from the 3/1,000 conditional null exceedances.
limit: This report uses the wider 2016 +/-3.5 core-width window; it must not be mixed with later +/-2.5 global-calibration definitions.

title: 2016 narrower-window comparison
question: Does a lower observed upper limit imply better signal sensitivity?
accomplishment: Changing +/-3.5u to +/-2u lowers the median 2016 observed limit by 9.64%, but paired response falls to 0.877-0.922 from 0.998-1.001. Response-adjusted spread ratios are 0.998-1.030.
limit: A five-mass, one-strength conditional test does not establish a universal sensitivity gain or coverage; the later +/-2.5u global study is a distinct fixed choice.

title: Complete-scan raw-statistic calibration
question: How often does a whole background scan reach the observed raw maximum?
accomplishment: Ran 1,024 coherent scans with 2016 +/-2.5u, 2021 [-4,+3]u and unchanged 2015 Gaussian. Direct raw-maximum p values are 0.0663, 0.2341 and 0.1980 for 2016, 2021 and common coupling.
limit: Finite-grid, fixed-source calibration omits source uncertainty and earlier method/window selection. A separate three-search family test is supplementary.

title: Raw versus local-calibrated ordering audit
question: Why can the selected combined mass depend on scan ordering?
accomplishment: Reused existing arrays to show that the combined raw maximum is at 67 MeV while the minimum local rank is at 68 MeV; no new fits were run.
limit: An audit of the original ensemble is not independent validation. It motivated the separated A/B procedure in v6.4.4.

title: Independent local-to-global calibration
question: What is the scan-wide probability after allowing for mass-dependent local behavior?
accomplishment: A fixes the local maps (1,024 scans); independent B validates minimum mapped p (1,024 scans). Combined: 75/1,024, add-one p=0.07415, 95% interval [0.05804,0.09095].
limit: The joint fit has one common coupling. This is not the maximum across three searches. The combined local rank hits 1/1025; B ties count inclusively. Source/map uncertainty and prior selection remain outside scope.

title: Mass correlation and the look-elsewhere effect
question: How much do overlapping mass hypotheses reduce the trial penalty?
accomplishment: Reused unchanged A/B scans. Combined direct p=0.074 versus an empirical independent-mass control of 0.133; simple single-year resolution counts understate the observed thresholds' penalty.
limit: Correlation bands describe variation across mass pairs, not confidence intervals. The independence control is counterfactual; no new probability or limit replaces v6.4.4.

title: APEX contour comparison
question: Do the supplied APEX curves align with the HPS local structures?
accomplishment: Digitized the supplied screenshots and compared the 155-250 MeV overlap. No common integer mass has both supplied local probabilities below 0.1.
limit: The APEX source, confidence level and resolution-axis units remain unresolved; contour crossings and nearby minima are not combined significance or exclusion.

title: Initial presentation revision
question: Which presentation material is ready to revisit and explain?
accomplishment: Updated the 15 instructed slides in a 79-slide snapshot; added kernel, extraction, validation, CLs, exposure and global-calibration explanations.
limit: This is a dated saved snapshot. Consult the next two revisions for later slide numbers and refinements.

title: Presentation validation and speaker scripts
question: Which presentation material is ready to revisit and explain?
accomplishment: Added two validation slides (85 total), revised eight instructed slides, and saved concise/extended spoken explanations and selected-mass sideband checks.
limit: The fitted-sideband check does not validate prediction in the excluded signal window; the 78 MeV example was already selected.

title: Latest saved presentation follow-up
question: Which presentation material is ready to revisit and explain?
accomplishment: Updated slides 13, 14 and 29. All 42 observed sideband-deviance values lie inside their pointwise 90% conditional bands; saved residual guidance, BEST conversion explanation and pixel-preservation evidence.
limit: Neighboring centers reuse the same spectra, so pointwise agreement is not a global goodness-of-fit or predictive-coverage result. The saved deck is a snapshot, not a live-deck verification.
